sentences.text:
Samid Sk vs Unknown on 4 December, 2025
60. 04.12.2025
Court
No.8 (Tanmoy)
 In The High Court At Calcutta
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Ia No: Cran/1/2024
 In
 Cra (Db)/211/2024

In Re: an application under Section 389 of the Code of Criminal  Procedure, 1973 / Section 430 BNSS, 2023 against the  judgment and order dated 04.11.2024, passed by the learned  Additional Sessions Judge, Kandi, Murshidabad in ST No.
 01(05)/2011 corresponding to SC No. 132/2010, under Section  376 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

In the matter of: - SAMID SK.
 Ms. Minoti Gomes  Mr. Md. Hafiz Ali  ...for the applicant/appellant  Ms. Zareen J. Khan, Jr. Govt.

Adv . 
 Ms. Paromita Sahu  ...for the S  Mr. Sanjib Seth  Ms. Soumi Chakraborty  ...for the de facto complainant.

Dictated by Apurba Sinha Ray, J.
1.

This is an application for suspension of sentence pending disposal of the appeal against the judgment and order dated July 4, 2024, passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kandi,
Murshidabad in ST No. 01(05)/2011 corresponding to SC No. 132/2010, under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

2. Learned Counsel for the applicant submits that post conviction the present applicant, namely,
SAMID SK., is in custody for one year and four months.
There are several loopholes in the prosecution case and evidence and there is fair chance of his success in the appeal.
The victim's evidence is not reliable since she did not speak about the time and date of the incident.
She remained silent for 10 months before lodging any complaint against the applicant.
As there is no chance of an early hearing of the appeal, the applicant may be enlarged on bail by suspending the sentence on any condition.
3. Learned Counsel for the de facto complainant opposes the prayer.

According to him, at the time of committing the offence, the victim girl was a minor and she was a maid- servant at the house of the Samid Sk vs Unknown on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9654844/
1 applicant.
On the pretext of marrying her, the applicant committed sexual offences with the minor victim.

4. Learned Counsel for the State submits that there is sufficient incriminating evidence showing the complicity of the present applicant and the learned Trial Judge has rightly convicted and sentenced the applicant, in accordance with law.
5. We have gone through the materials on record including the evidence of the victim.
We find that there is incriminating evidence against the applicant.
If the evidence of the victim is reliable, there is no need of further corroboration of such evidence.
6. In view of the materials on record, we are not inclined to extend the privilege of suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the applicant at this stage.
7. The application being IA No: CRAN/1/2024 is accordingly dismissed.
In Re: CRA (DB) 211 of 2024 8.
From a departmental note dated November 21, 2025, we find that paper book in connection with this appeal is ready and the same was served on the State on November 11, 2025.
The applicant's learned Advocate would be at liberty to collect the paper book from the department.

9. Place the appeal under the appropriate heading in the Combined Monthly list of January, 2026.
10.
Criminal Section is directed to make available certified copies of this order to the parties, if applied for, upon compliance with all requisite formalities.

(Apurba Sinha Ray, J.) (Arijit Banerjee, J.)
